evals.prompt: I run growth at Tellurian Ops, we sell a workflow tool to facilities teams. ACV is $4,200. Direct sales have been flat at about $90k new ARR per quarter for four quarters straight and we've missed plan twice. Our CRO thinks a reseller channel is the answer - he wants four tiers (Bronze through Platinum), a 30% margin table copied off a competitor's partner page, a partner portal, and 100 signed resellers in year one. I've been asked to write the program plan. Where do I start on the tier criteria and the margin table?
evals.expected_output: A refusal to design the requested tiers and margin table, replaced by a readiness-gate verdict of 'not yet' that names the disqualifiers, states what must change, names referral-only as the lighter motion that still fits, and stops there.
expectations: Concludes the honest answer is 'not yet' and declines to design the tier criteria or the margin table as asked
Names at least three separate disqualifiers rather than resting on one
Identifies the flat, non-repeatable direct motion as a disqualifier, stating that partners amplify a working motion rather than fix a broken one
Identifies expecting partners to solve a growth problem as a disqualifier in its own right
Identifies the $4,200 ACV as too low to fund a reseller motion, explaining that the partner's own cost of sale has to clear before the vendor's does
Flags the absence of a named executive sponsor as a disqualifier, or asks who the named executive sponsor is before proceeding any further
States that any single disqualifier is enough to return 'not yet' - the gate is not scored, averaged, or traded off
Names referral-only as the lighter motion that still fits at this ACV
Flags copying the competitor's 30% margin table as a structural mistake rather than a number to tune
States what must change before the gate can be re-run, covering direct-motion repeatability and the ACV or margin headroom
Does not produce a four-tier Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum ladder
Does not set a recruitment target of 100 partners or otherwise treat signed-partner count as the success metric

evals.prompt: Bellweather Analytics here - B2B data quality product, $38k ACV, gross margin 79%, direct sales are repeatable (61 closed deals in 18 months with three reps running the same playbook). Our COO Priya Raman is the named sponsor. Four boutique data consultancies already implement us for their own clients with no agreement in place. We can't fund a new hire this year; I'd be running this alone alongside my current job, maybe six hours a week. The board wants a partner-sourced number on the books by the end of Q2, five months out. Which partner motions should we run? I'm assuming we do referral, reseller, tech integrations and an SI program and just phase them.
evals.expected_output: A motion selection that states the efficiency ordering explicitly, deletes motions the constraints rule out with reopen triggers attached, re-ranks against the consultancies and the team-of-one constraint, and lands on a minimum viable set rather than a phased rollout of all four.
expectations: Refuses to run all four motions and picks a minimum viable set instead of phasing every motion
States the efficiency ordering of the motion menu out loud rather than leaving it implied by list order
Gives the default efficiency order as referral > technology > services-SI > reseller
Presents at least one further axis - effort, value ceiling, time-to-effect, or compliance cost - whose order disagrees with the efficiency order
Deletes reseller outright rather than scheduling it for a later phase, citing the absence of fundable standing headcount
Deletes services-SI on the same headcount constraint, or explicitly resolves the conflict between that deletion and the consultancy-driven promotion
Records a reopen trigger alongside each deleted motion rather than leaving it deleted with no stated condition
Uses the five-month board deadline to promote referral, saying that a hard date inside two quarters is the answer that moved it
Notes that the four consultancies already implementing the product promote services-SI, because the recruitment effort is already spent
States that a team of one collapses the menu to referral plus at most one integration
Names the condition that would promote reseller anyway: reaching a named segment or geography is the stated goal of the program and standing headcount is funded
Names the condition that would promote services-SI anyway: implementation appears as a named reason in lost or stalled deals, not merely that an SI relationship exists
Chooses motions before any Ideal Partner Profile or formal partner-scoring work rather than starting from a partner profile

evals.prompt: Kestrel Freight Systems. We're standing up our first partner program - referral only for now, maybe eight partners by next summer. I've drafted the ladder: Bronze at 0 referrals, Silver at 3, Gold at 10, Platinum at 25, with a nicer logo badge and priority support at each step. Can you tighten up the criteria thresholds and tell me what benefits belong at each tier?
evals.expected_output: A refusal to set the count or design per-tier criteria and benefits here, limited instead to whether to tier and what the differentiation is for, with the count, criteria and benefit design handed to the tiering skill and the four-tier ladder challenged.
expectations: Declines to set the tier count or design the per-tier criteria and benefits in this answer
Hands tier count, criteria, and benefit design to mbfinotti/partnerships-skills@partner-tiering
Explains that fixing a tier count here risks re-papering signed partner agreements once the tiering skill re-derives the count from partner-base size
Limits its own decision to whether to tier at all and what the differentiation is for
States that a tier exists only when something measurable changes at its boundary
States that criteria with no benefits delta is a leaderboard nobody plays
States that a benefits delta with no criteria is favoritism wearing a logo
Challenges the four-tier ladder for a program this size rather than accepting it, noting four tiers is usually vanity
Flags a logo badge and priority support as cosmetic differentiation with no economic change at the boundary
Does not present an efficiency ranking over tier counts

evals.prompt: Orlando at Vantablack Logistics. We sell a $26k ACV routing platform, 68% gross margin. I pulled our closest competitor's partner page and they pay resellers 30%, so I've put 30% in our model too and rounded our referral fee to 15% of year one. Finance has signed off on the total spend. What else do I need in the economics section before we launch?
evals.expected_output: A rejection of the copied margin, replaced by the envelope method: derive margin from the task the partner takes over, model the partner's own side on the stated deal size, compare channel cost-of-sale to direct CAC, fit total cost inside gross margin, and set direct-rep comp neutrality now.
expectations: Rejects the copied 30% competitor margin as a structural mistake rather than validating it against benchmark bands
States that partner margin must come out of a cost the partner takes off the vendor's hands
States that paying margin for work the vendor would have done anyway buys nothing from the partner
Asks or specifies which operational task the partner is actually taking over before any number is set
Models the partner's own side, computing what 30% leaves the partner on a $26k deal (roughly $7,800) against their acquisition and delivery costs
Compares the resulting channel cost-of-sale against direct CAC, naming a channel costlier than direct as a strategy tax rather than leverage
Requires total program cost to fit inside gross margin
Sets direct-rep compensation neutrality on partner-touched deals now, at architecture time, rather than leaving it as a later fix
Names misaligned direct-rep compensation as a root cause of channel conflict rather than a symptom of it
Requires cost-to-serve per partner to be tracked from day one, not just partner-generated revenue
Hands per-partner modeling to mbfinotti/partnerships-skills@partner-economics rather than doing it here

evals.prompt: We launched our channel program in February. It's now September and our CRO wants it shut down - 14 partners signed, two registered deals, one closed for $31k. He's comparing it to our direct team, which turns a lead into closed business in about 70 days. I have one meeting on Thursday to save it. What do I tell him?
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis naming the month-seven judgment against a 70-day direct cycle as a horizon error, with the horizon reset placed first in the fix order and justified on cost, plus the year-1/2/3 ladder to replace the current expectation.
expectations: Identifies the month-seven judgment against a 70-day direct cycle as a horizon error, a structural problem rather than a performance problem
Names the horizon reset as the first fix to make, ahead of any other remediation
Justifies the horizon reset leading on cost: one leadership conversation, and it stops the program being killed before any other fix can land
States the ranking of remediations out loud rather than implying it by list order
Gives year 1 as leading indicators only, naming at least two of partners activated, deals registered, time-to-first-deal, or enablement completion
Gives year 2 as meaningful partner-sourced pipeline
Gives year 3 as material revenue contribution
States that partner relationship maturity takes roughly two to three years, so little net revenue in year 1 is expected rather than a failure signal
Does not recommend recruiting more partners as the answer to the low deal count
States that the horizon decision belongs in the architecture at design time, not as a rescue argued after the fact

evals.prompt: Inherited a two-year-old channel program at Northgate Instruments. 214 signed partners, 19 did anything at all last quarter. Our direct AEs quietly steer deals away from partners because their quota relief drops 40% when a partner is on the deal. Partners have stopped submitting registrations since we took three accounts back as house accounts in May. We allocated $400k of market development funds and $37k got claimed. We run a single tier, no metals. Exec team already knows this is a three-year build and isn't threatening to kill it. Give me the fix list in the order I should work it.
evals.expected_output: An explicit remediation ordering with the rows that do not apply to this user deleted rather than demoted, conflict and registration policy first among what remains, comp neutrality named highest-value but placed later on cost, and each symptom traced to its structural cause.
expectations: States the fix ranking out loud as an explicit order rather than leaving it implied by list order
Deletes the horizon reset from this user's list because leadership already holds a three-year expectation, rather than demoting it to last
Deletes the tier rebuild because the program runs a single tier
Places conflict and registration policy first among the fixes that still apply
Places comp neutrality below activation-over-recruitment and funds mechanics in the working order, despite naming it the highest-value fix
Justifies comp neutrality's placement by its cost: a mid-year compensation change, slow and politically expensive
Traces the stalled registrations to the house-account carve-outs and prescribes honoring registration without carve-outs
Traces the 214-signed / 19-active gap to recruitment being tracked instead of activation, and stops recruiting rather than adding partners
Traces the unclaimed funds to market-development funds designed apart from deal registration, and puts both under one owner
Proposes automatic registration approval for funded leads as part of the funds fix
Names the 40% quota-relief cut as an architecture decision rather than a behavior problem with the AEs
Prescribes a mutual action plan per partner as part of the activation fix

evals.prompt: Here's our partner one-pager draft for Saltmarsh Identity: 'Partners commit a dedicated named rep, complete our two-day certification within 60 days, register every opportunity within 5 business days, and maintain $250k annual influenced revenue to stay in good standing.' We're taking it to about 40 agencies next month. Can you sharpen the copy and suggest the outreach sequence?
evals.expected_output: A stop on the outreach, with the one-pager identified as all ask and no give, the give-before-ask order supplied, and a written Partner Hypothesis required and validated against 2-3 real prospective partners against a stated proceed threshold before any 40-agency push.
expectations: Declines to sharpen the outreach copy or build the 40-agency sequence as the next step
Identifies the one-pager as entirely vendor asks with no partner give
States the give-before-ask rule: the program must give before it may ask
Lists the gives in order, covering a clear way to make money, training to sell well, tools to track activity, and vendor air cover or conflict resolution, before any ask
Requires a one-sentence partner value proposition answering what is in this for the partner
Requires a written Partner Hypothesis of roughly one to two pages naming the target partner type, why they would engage, and the expected economics
Names the Partner Hypothesis as a practitioner framework with attribution rather than presenting it as a universal standard
Requires validation against 2-3 real prospective partners before anything is built on it, rather than going to 40 at once
States the proceed threshold: at least two prospective partners confirm the joint value proposition and a shared customer overlap exists
States that the validation record is not optional and must name who it was tested on and what each confirmed or contradicted
Defers formal scored partner profiling until recruiting volume justifies it, using the validated hypothesis for the first cohort instead

evals.prompt: Copperline Bikes - we make e-cargo bikes, sold direct online, average order $3,900. We want a dealer network: independent bike shops that stock, sell and service us. I want exclusive postcode territories so shops actually invest, a required shop layout and staff script, and I'd like to reuse the SaaS partner program structure my last company ran (registered/silver/gold, deal registration, MDF). I figured we'd also ship dealers the full 180-page brand and operations manual on day one. Sound right?
evals.expected_output: A B2C fork: the territory-plus-operational-control combination flagged as franchising needing counsel, deal registration correctly distinguished from a territory, the opposite documentation defaults named, consumer-specific requirements raised, and what genuinely stays identical named.
expectations: Flags that exclusive territories combined with a mandated shop layout and staff scripts drift toward franchising, and recommends franchise counsel rather than a partner program template
Names franchising as a separate legal discipline with a mandated pre-sale disclosure document, citing the FTC Franchise Rule where the US applies
States that B2B deal registration protects a named account for a time window and is not a substitute for a geographic territory held in perpetuity
States that documentation depth is the opposite default on the two sides, so the 180-page manual fits a franchise-shaped model and would be a named failure mode in B2B SaaS
Names the deliberately minimal B2B launch kit it contrasts against, covering pitch deck, demo script, pricing sheet, one or two battle cards, and a case study
Distinguishes point-of-sale consumer attribution from B2B's multi-month pipeline attribution, and notes that reward triggers and fraud exposure change with it
Raises front-line mindshare: winning the individual floor rep's point-of-sale recommendation, often worth more than any rebate structure
Raises dealer-locator findability on the vendor's own site as a consumer-side requirement with no meaningful B2B equivalent
Names what stays identical across both sides, including deep-qualifying a small first cohort before scaling recruitment and modeling economics from the partner's side first
States that a compelling economic offer, not marketing, is what recruits on both sides
Poses the consumer-side fork questions, including whether the reward fires at signup or only at verified sale and the sharper fraud trade-off that comes with instant conversion

evals.prompt: Prepping the kickoff for our brand-new partner program at Halcyon Grid. My plan: (1) convene a partner advisory board of 20 people to shape it, (2) run a two-day journey-mapping workshop across the twelve partner personas we brainstormed, (3) use the numbers to get budget - I've got '70% of partnerships fail within two years' and 'partner-involved deals close 46% faster' in the deck already. Which workshop do I book first?
evals.expected_output: The advisory board deleted for a program with no partners yet, journey mapping placed last with its invalidation risk named, partner-hypothesis validation put first as the only format that can stop the program, and both quoted statistics refused as established fact.
expectations: Deletes the partner advisory board from a from-scratch program because there are no partners with activity to convene yet, and names the condition that returns it to the menu
States the collaboration-format ranking out loud rather than leaving it implied
Gives partner-hypothesis validation as the leading format, ahead of any facilitated workshop
Justifies that lead by it being the only format whose output can stop the program
Places partner journey mapping last, because it only pays once motions and partner types are fixed
Warns that a journey map run before the architecture maps a journey the architecture then invalidates
Requires a named journey owner appointed before any mapping workshop, and names the failure of unowned sessions
Challenges the twelve personas, requiring the persona count be disciplined down before anything is mapped
Refuses to present '70% of partnerships fail within two years' as established fact, identifying it as anecdotal or secondhand
Refuses to present the 46%-faster deal-velocity claim as established fact, identifying it as a single vendor's survey of its own ecosystem

Flags the shared-customer discovery sprint's compliance cost where it is raised: it exchanges customer lists between two companies, triggers mutual data-sharing terms, and a list that has crossed cannot be un-shared
Does not book the two-day journey-mapping workshop as the first action

evals.prompt: We've been round and round on this for three weeks at Ferrous Labs - $55k ACV data platform, 74% gross margin, direct motion is solid with two years of consistent quota attainment, and our CFO Dana Whitlock is sponsoring it. I need one document I can put in front of finance, legal and sales on Monday so they stop asking me questions. What goes in it and can you just write it?
evals.expected_output: A section-by-section build with candidate approaches and approval gates rather than a single unvalidated document, producing the Program Architecture Spec with every named line, a reason per line, and the three-condition pass threshold applied.
expectations: Presents the architecture section by section with an approval gate, rather than emitting the whole document unvalidated in one block
Offers 2-3 candidate approaches with trade-offs and an explicit recommendation per section, not a single option
Names the deliverable as a Program Architecture Spec and lists the lines it must carry
Includes a Readiness line covering direct-motion evidence, ACV band, gross-margin headroom, and the named executive sponsor
Includes a Partner value line carrying both the one-sentence proposition and a validation record naming 2-3 prospective partners and what each confirmed or contradicted
Includes a Motions line naming which motions were chosen, the order they were chosen in after re-ranking, and every motion a constraint deleted with the trigger that would reopen it
Includes a First cohort line with a target size around ten, a qualification bar, and an activation milestone per partner
Names the qualification bar as Capability, Capacity, Coverage, Commitment
Includes Tiers, Economics, Governance and Horizon lines, with Governance carrying an owner plus reporting line and the deal-registration/conflict policy status
States that every line of the spec carries a reason, so a bare decision such as an unexplained tier count is not acceptable

Applies the three-condition pass threshold - economics inside gross margin, partner value proposition survived contact with 2-3 real prospective partners, a named executive sponsor exists - and recommends not launching if no architecture passes
